data.name: Amad
data.gender_notes: Amad is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'A-M-D', meaning 'I promise' or 'I will remain'. The name Amad is often used to denote the concept of eternal and perpetual existence, or the idea of a promise kept. The name Amad carries the meaning “Eternity, Perpetuity” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Amad usually hope their child will grow to embody eternity, perpetuity and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that signifies the presence of God in one's life, a reminder of His constant generosity and love
data.etymology: Amad belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Eternity, Perpetuity.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Amad total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

In Islamic traditions, Amad is a reminder of God's promise to His creation - a promise of justice, peace, and a beautiful future in paradise for those who remain steadfast in their faith. The name reflects the concept of a covenant, or a strong commitment, that individuals and communities make with God, as well as with each other.

It serves as a reminder of our own promises and commitments to God, encouraging us to strive for personal growth, self-improvement, and a closer connection with the divine. In this way, the name Amad offers a constant source of inspiration and motivation for individuals seeking spiritual growth and connection.
